places.name: Point Isabel Regional Shoreline
places.rule_summary: Dogs may be off leash here as long as they are under their owner's control, except where posted. The district calls it its most dog-friendly park.
places.off_leash_notes: Carry a leash (6 ft max) and use it in parking lots and developed areas. Park-specific posted rules apply.
places.verified_by: claude (official page fetch), pending human review

photo.alt: Dirt path and cypress trees near the entrance of Point Isabel Regional Shoreline

park_wide: The park page mentions more than 2.5 miles of San Francisco Bay Trail in the vicinity of the park.
Dogs must be on a leash in parking lots and streets.

sources.label: East Bay Regional Park District: Point Isabel

places.name: Tilden Regional Park
places.rule_summary: District-wide rule: dogs may be off leash in open space and undeveloped areas if they are in view and under voice control, and must return to leash when called. Leash (6 ft max) is required in developed areas, parking lots, picnic areas, grazing areas and for the first 200 ft of a trailhead. Dogs are not allowed at the Tilden Nature Area, the Botanic Garden or the golf course.
places.off_leash_notes: This rule comes from the district-wide dogs page; this park has no park-specific rule listed there. Posted signs override.
places.verified_by: claude (official page fetch), pending human review

photo.alt: Hazy hills and trees seen from Selby Trail in Tilden Regional Park

park_wide: The park page says there are 39.41 miles of trails in Tilden Park. That is all trails, not only ones open to dogs.
Dogs must be on a leash on Nimitz Way.
Dogs are not allowed in the swim facility at Lake Anza.

sources.label: East Bay Regional Park District: Tilden

places.name: Redwood Regional Park
places.rule_summary: District-wide rule: dogs may be off leash in open space and undeveloped areas if they are in view and under voice control, and must return to leash when called. Leash (6 ft max) is required in developed areas, parking lots, picnic areas, grazing areas and for the first 200 ft of a trailhead. Dogs must be on leash in the Serpentine Prairie area (Dunn and Serpentine Prairie trails), and are not allowed in Redwood Arena or the Redwood Stream Protection Area.

places.name: Fort Funston
places.rule_summary: The Superintendent's Compendium lists Fort Funston for dogs leashed or under voice control, except the 12-acre closure in the northwest corner. Closed to dogs: the Habitat Protection Area, signed administrative areas, and the Coastal Trail at the Horse Trail / Great Highway intersection.
places.off_leash_notes: Voice control areas are defined by posted signs and park maps.
places.verified_by: claude (official page fetch), pending human review

photo.alt: Overlook at Fort Funston with a hang glider and the coastline

park_wide: The NPS page says its networked trails are ideal for accessible hiking, horseback riding and dog walking.
The loop trails are paved and wheelchair-accessible; the trails down to the beach are not.

places.name: Crissy Field

places.off_leash_notes: In the marked off-leash area, keep a leash in your possession and keep your dog under voice control.
